intro: One medium fried ikan kembung is about 200 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the fish itself, plus the oil absorbed during frying.

variants.name: Ikan kembung stuffed with fried sambal

diet: Yes, you can. Ikan kembung is a very diet-friendly lauk. It's high in protein and has good omega-3 fats. Even the plain turmeric-fried version is still low in calories compared to many other dishes. Just watch the oily berlada sauce and too much rice.
tips: Choose plain turmeric-fried ikan kembung over the sambal-coated one.
If there's a choice, go for ikan bakar or asam pedas.
Pair it with vegetables and half rice for a balanced plate.

swap.name: Ikan kembung bakar with air asam
swap.why: No frying oil but still tasty. Air asam adds flavour without many extra calories.

faq.q: Does ikan kembung have a lot of bones?
faq.a: It has some fine bones, but not too many. The middle bone is easy to remove, so it's okay for kids too with supervision.

faq.q: How do I fry ikan kembung so it doesn't break apart?
faq.a: Pat the fish dry, marinate with turmeric and salt, and make sure the oil is hot. Don't flip it too early.

faq.q: Ikan kembung or salmon, which is better?
faq.a: Both are rich in omega-3. Ikan kembung is much cheaper and easy to find at Malaysian markets, so it's a great everyday choice.
